Jim Barne and Kit Buchan wrote the songs and the book for this rom-com two-hander, and they begin “Two Strangers” with real promise. The young man Dougal (Tutty) is newly arrived at JFK from London and eager to meet his American father for the very first time. Dad’s getting married and the bride’s sister, Robin (Pitts), picks him up at the airport.
It's also one of the best new musicals of the year.
In a season crowded with gaudy overindulgence, this small, sweet musical carries its multi-layered cake with surprising elegance.
Utterly charming and winsomely quirky, this show evokes laughter and joy in equal measures, while also contending with moments of substance and painful truth.
As the icing on the cake, not only have they fallen in love with each other but we’ve fallen in love with them as well.
It's also one of the more entertaining, in part because it relies on solid writing rather than distracting gimmicks.
The show might refer to itself as a musical comedy, but it is closer to a play with music, and an outstanding one at that.
This would be a thumbs up date night show no matter your age.
Warm, witty, and easy to enjoy.

While its titular parenthetical suggests a much less hefty musical, Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) does encourage a rewarding lift: to appreciate passion in the present, even if it can’t be safeguarded.
If you are looking for great structure and exhilarating drama, look elsewhere.
